coherence.title: Coherence takes out the dry ground
coherence.what: At L-band smooth dry ground is as dark as water. Over 12 days water loses its radar phase and dry ground keeps it, so NISAR's coherence tells them apart. Off: every dark pixel (HH below -15 dB). On: only dark pixels with low coherence (below 0.25) stay water. The amber layer, to lay on top if wanted, is the dark ground coherence takes out.

items.rule: the date with a coherence pair and an optical answer key at least 90 % clear that has the most dark ground

photo.source: Sentinel-2 L2A true colour (visual), Element 84 Earth Search
photo.credit: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2026, Element 84 Earth Search

caption: 30 Jun: 2,022 ha outside permanent water look as dark as water to the radar.
Coherence over the 12 days before (18 Jun to 30 Jun) keeps 206 ha as water and takes out the 1,816 ha that kept their coherence, as dry ground.
Judged by the optical map of the day: darkness alone calls 4 % of the dry ground water, coherence 0.3 %. The price: coherence finds 8 % of the open water, darkness alone 19 %.

dark_ha.what: dark (HH below -15 dB) in the window, outside the sea and permanent water

kept_ha.what: of it with low coherence (below 0.25): kept as water

removed_ha.what: of it coherent: called dry ground by the rule

coh_false_water.what: of it the coherence rule calls water

context.text: Albufera is one of the three sites the coherence cut of 0.25 was chosen on, so these numbers are not a test. Pego-Oliva and Doñana are test sites.
Across 26 dates at Doñana, coherence cuts the false water from 32 % to 5 % of the dry ground.

dark_false_water.what: of the optical dry ground darkness alone calls water

context.text: In the Pego-Oliva marsh, where water keeps some coherence, it does not help: IoU 0.306 with coherence against 0.340 for darkness alone.

soil.title: Soil wetness before the storm
soil.what: NISAR soil moisture of the top soil (L3 SME2, a provisional product, not yet validated), as stored for the spatial model by pipeline/soil_moisture.py: every pass over the site, the passes of one day averaged, on 200 m cells. The last dates before the DANA of 18 to 19 Oct; dates are compared on the cells both have.
caption: 16 Oct, two days before the storm: half of the land read below 0.23 m³/m³ of soil moisture, nine in ten cells below 0.28.
Of the 17 earlier dates, from 18 Jun on, 10 read drier on the same cells.
The ground was not soaked when the storm came: it read within the range of the summer, below its wettest date (30 Jun, 0.30 on the same cells).

last_median.what: median soil moisture of the land on 16 Oct

last_p90.what: nine in ten cells read below this

earlier_drier.what: earlier dates that read drier than the last on the cells both have
